correctness.rationale: The geodesic-square convolution has constant term π²/12 and nonzero multipliers (−1)^j/(2j²) on density coefficients in the stated normalization. With z=e^(2it), a nonconstant degree-d loss shifted to vanish at its minimum becomes a polynomial of degree at most 2d after multiplication by z^d. A root of order 2m implies d≥m. At d=m the polynomial is proportional to (z−z0)^(2m); the proportionality before removing the Laurent factor may have a phase/sign, and (z−z0)^2/(zz0)=−2(1−cos(2(t−t0))) makes the resulting positive real amplitude explicit. Inversion can also be checked from πψ(t)=1−F''(t+π/2)/2, by differentiating the geodesic-square kernel across its antipodal cusp. For F=constant+ε(1−cos2t)^m this is exactly 1+εR_m(cos2t). R_m' has the sign of m²c−m²+3m−1 on (−1,1), and its minimum at c=1−3/m+1/m² is −1/ε_m. Since the loss requires ε>0, the strict positivity interval follows. Angular averaging gives the stated F(0); the loss vanishes only at the centered point and starts at order 2m. The optional empirical limit agrees with the circular statement after doubling and rescaling angles; the relevant Hotz–Huckemann pointer is Theorem 4.2(ii) in the accessed arXiv text, rather than the source's ‘Theorem 3’.
